name: TextEditor
summary: A bounded rich-text editor with a portable Mux document value.

useWhen: Writing a short formatted note, with the default simple toolbar
Authoring a longer document with the advanced toolbar, when the application supplies its own link, image, and generate handlers
Formatting from the application's own toolbar, with toolbar false, the formatting the editor reports, and its commands
avoidWhen: Editing plain text; use TextArea for several lines or TextField for one
Composing a message to send; use PromptComposer
Showing Markdown that is not edited; use Markdown

obligations: Expose the accessible name, descriptions, required, disabled, read-only, and invalid state on the editable content.
Expose toolbar button names and pressed state.
Keep the editable region keyboard operable.
Expose the color popup as a dialog with a labelled custom color field.
Expose the selection actions bar as a named toolbar whose controls, field, and expanded state have names, and announce pending, review, and failure states in a polite live region.
Keep focus in the editor when the selection actions bar appears, and let the keyboard enter and leave the bar without losing the selection.
Under forced colours, draw the editable content's edge and keyboard focus in system colours.
Move focus into the editable content only when the application asks, with autoFocus or the handle, and without scrolling the page when asked not to.

behavior: The document is either controlled by the application with value or managed by the editor from defaultValue.
A document contains blocks only.
Paragraphs and headings contain inline text and hard breaks.
Lists contain nonempty list-item sequences beginning with a paragraph.
Block quotes contain nonempty block sequences.
Code blocks contain plain text.
Text is never empty: isTextEditorDocument returns false for empty text, and normalizeTextEditorDocument drops it.
Horizontal rules and images are atomic blocks.
Safe marks preserve bold, italic, underline, strike, code, links, colors, font families, and font sizes.
Link URLs must be absolute http, https, or mailto URLs, and image URLs must be absolute http or https URLs.
URLs with a username or password, or with control characters, are rejected.
isTextEditorDocument returns true only for a value that exactly matches the document grammar.
Unknown keys, unsupported nodes and marks, and unsafe URLs make isTextEditorDocument return false.

normalizeTextEditorDocument returns a valid document and drops what the grammar does not allow, such as unsupported nodes, marks, and unsafe URLs; a link whose URL it drops keeps its text, and an image its description.
A value that is not a document, or has nothing left after normalizing, becomes a document with one empty paragraph.
TextEditor normalizes value and defaultValue, and onChange receives a normalized document.
onChange runs for edits the editor accepts, not at mount, when disabled or readOnly changes, or when value changes from outside.

A value from outside that replaces the content is applied as given, with no address in it linked, also when undo or redo brings it back, and is one undo step of its own, apart from the typing just before and after it.

A document from outside is compared with the content as the editor holds both, so marks in another order, text split where its marks stay the same, and attributes left at their defaults, such as a numbered list's start, replace nothing.
The simple toolbar renders Bold, Italic, Underline, Color, alignment, and Bullet list controls with separators.
The advanced toolbar adds font selects, Link, Image, and Generate with AI.
Color opens a 16-swatch popup with a custom hex ColorField.
Image requests a durable http(s) image URL when no onImageRequest callback is supplied.
Without onLinkRequest, Link asks for an address in a browser prompt, and Generate with AI does nothing without onGenerate.
Consumers can own file uploads and insert their durable URL through onImageRequest.
Toolbar requests use finite actions and can be controlled with onGenerate.
onLinkRequest, onImageRequest, and onColorRequest each receive an object of actions to apply the result: setLink and unsetLink, insertImage, and setColor.
The ref is a handle with focus(options) and execute(command).
focus() focuses the editable content a frame later and scrolls its selection into view; focus({ preventScroll: true }) focuses it at once and scrolls nothing.
execute takes a command object: bold, italic, underline, strike, code, bulletList, orderedList, blockquote, codeBlock, paragraph, horizontalRule, unlink, and generate need only a type.

heading also takes a level from 1 to 6, text takes the text to insert, align, color, fontFamily, and fontSize take a value, link takes an href and an optional text, and image takes a src and an optional alt.

A mark is on in the formatting at a caret where the next typed text takes it, and over a range where all the selected text has it. The built-in toolbar shows a caret's marks the same way, so neither shows a mark in a block that takes none, such as a code block, whatever a shortcut held there. Over a range, bold, italic, underline, strike, and code switch as their shortcuts and the built-in toolbar do, which count inline code as having the mark, so over bold text and inline code the formatting shows bold off and bold takes it off.

heading and paragraph set every selected text block; where every selected block already is that kind and level they return true and do nothing at all: they change nothing, add no undo step, and leave focus where it is.

text replaces the selection with plain text that takes the marks typed text would take, and keeps the caret in view; a line break becomes a hard break, and stays a line break in a code block, and the next typed text keeps those marks after a trailing one.

Each command that changes the document is one undo step of its own, apart from the typing before and after it; one that changes nothing, such as an alignment a block already has, adds no undo step and splits none, also during an input method's composition.
An address typed or inserted as text becomes a link only where the link command would accept the address the link gets.

A pasted or dropped link or image, and an image typed as Markdown, keeps its URL only where the link or image command would accept it; otherwise a link keeps its text, an image its description, and a typed image the text typed.
A caret is in a link when the next typed text would take it: at the link's end but not at its start, even where the link starts a paragraph.
At a caret in a link, link gives the whole link the new address, and unlink removes the whole link; both keep the other marks held for typing.

link with text puts the text, linked, at a caret, in place of the selected text, or in place of the whole link at a caret in one, and replaces a Select All selection with one paragraph holding it; at a caret the text takes the marks held there, and the caret follows it and the next typed text is not linked, also after an undo and redo of it, where the text joined a link to the same address too.
link applies nowhere in inline code or a code block.

execute returns true when the command applied and false when it did not, for example when the editor is disabled or read-only, a URL is not allowed, the character limit refuses the edit, or a mark cannot go on the selection, as in a code block or on inline code.
limit is a number of characters of the editor's plain text: a fraction is rounded down, and a negative, infinite, or omitted limit means no limit.
A break between blocks counts as two characters.
An edit that would leave the text longer than limit is refused and is not passed to onChange, whether the document is controlled or managed by the editor.
A controlled editor keeps showing value after a refused edit.
A refused edit adds no undo step, and undo and redo are never refused by the limit.
The hint under the editor shows how many characters are left and updates after every edit, including a change to value.
A paste is measured after Markdown such as **bold** becomes formatting; one that still does not fit is refused whole and is not shortened to fit.
A Markdown shortcut typed by hand is judged as each character is typed, so its closing character is refused when the text already fills limit, even though the formatted text would fit.
A value or defaultValue longer than limit is shown as given, and an edit is accepted only if it brings the text within limit or leaves it no longer than before.
TextEditor submits no value with a form and takes no part in native form validation, so required does not stop a form from submitting.
errorMessage shows its message and also marks the editor invalid.
The editor renders its editable content on the client after mount, so on the server neither onReady nor autoFocus runs.
onReady runs once for each editor once its editable content is in the page.
autoFocus focuses the editable content without scrolling when it is ready, if the editor is editable.

onFormattingChange receives the formatting at the selection when the editor is ready, and again whenever a selection move, a mark held for typing, or an edit changes it, never for an unchanged one; a command its callback runs is reported too, and a callback added later receives the formatting at once.

The formatting holds plain values: empty, the bold, italic, underline, strike, and code marks, the link address, the kind of text block and heading level, the nearest list, and whether a quote holds the selection.
A mark counts for selected text when all of it carries the mark, and at a caret when the next typed text would.
The block, list, and quote come from the text blocks whose content the selection covers, so a range over different kinds of block has no block.
minRows and maxRows bound the content's height in lines of its own line height, plus its padding; it grows with its text between them and then scrolls inside.
A fraction of a row is rounded down, a count below 1 is ignored, and maxRows is never less than minRows.
Without minRows the content keeps its default least height, unless maxRows is lower.
normalizeTextEditorUrl(value, kind) returns the address as the link or image command stores it, or null when that command would refuse it.
When bubbleMenu is enabled, a selection-driven Bold, Italic, Underline, and Link toolbar appears only for a nonempty selection and dismisses when the selection collapses.
The bubble menu is separate from the floating toolbar position.
Providing onSelectionRequest enables selection actions: a bar anchored under a nonempty selection.
The bar flips above the selection and stays inside the viewport.
The bar shows while the editor is editable and focused or the bar has focus.
The bar never takes focus and keeps the selected range painted while focus is in the bar.
The bar hides when the editor is disabled or read-only.
The bar holds a Describe edits field, the caller-supplied selectionActions with their icons, and a More actions control that expands overflow actions inline.
The Describe edits field sends on Enter, never during IME composition.
Typing replaces the actions with a Send control.
selectionInstruction false removes the field.
An action or instruction calls onSelectionRequest with the request and a controller.
The controller holds a snapshot of the selected text and document, an AbortSignal, replace, insertAfter, and close.
A returned promise shows the pending text (pendingLabel or Editing…) with a Cancel control.
A rejection shows a fixed failure message with Try again and Dismiss.
replace and insertAfter apply once, and return false when the request is stale, aborted, over limit, invalid, or the editor is disabled or read-only.
A string is plain text taking the formatting at the start of the selection, for insertAfter too; a document keeps its own formatting.
An edit or formatting change of the selected range, a controlled value change, Escape, Cancel, a new request, close, or unmount aborts the signal.
close also hides the bar until the selection changes, while keeping any applied edit.
After an edit applies, the new content stays highlighted with Keep, Discard, and Try again.
Keep ends the review, Discard undoes the edit exactly and reselects the original range, and Try again discards and resends the same request.
The edit is one undo step, and Discard leaves no extra step.
Alt+F10 from the editor moves focus into the bar.
Arrow keys, Home, and End move between the controls of the bar, and Escape or Tab return focus to the editor with the selection intact.
Escape in the editor hides the bar until the selection changes, or cancels a pending request.
accessibility: The editable content carries its name and form-like states.
Formatting actions expose named toggle buttons.
The color dialog and custom ColorField expose their names to assistive technology.
The selection formatting toolbar exposes named controls.

The selection actions toolbar exposes named actions, a named Describe edits field, an expanded state on More actions, and a busy state while a request runs, and a polite live region announces pending, review, and failure states.
Under forced colours the editable content draws its edge as a ButtonText outline and its focus as a Highlight outline.
